GoldbachStacks

Goldbach's conjecture as a building problem with prime stacks
Proved in Leanring 2Gaps between survivors and between primes

Original to this project. Each odd prime is a stack two wide with one point sticking up (3 is height 1, 5 height 2, 7 height 3, 11 height 5). Two stacks put together make twice their total height plus 2, so building every pair of stacks reaches the target heights. Proved here: the stacks never leave a gap exactly when Goldbach's conjecture holds, and so does the frontier form (as the stacks arrive in order, every target up to a new stack's height is already built from the stacks before it). These are equivalences only; Goldbach's conjecture itself stays open. Also proved: at the wheel of size 3 every stack above height 1 leaves remainder 0 or 2, never 1, and at any single wheel the surviving stacks, taken in pairs, reach every remainder, so no one wheel can force a gap. Resting on CRT, the same holds for the combined cycle of all the wheels below any bound at once: the good pairs chosen wheel by wheel join into one pair for the whole cycle. The open part is stated exactly as the window statement (window_no_gap, never claimed): every target is two heights, from 1 up to one less than the target, whose stacks survive every wheel up to the square root of twice the target plus 1. That range is far shorter than the combined cycle of those wheels, which is why the combined-cycle result does not reach it; the window statement is proved equivalent to the stack picture and to Goldbach's conjecture.

Published sources

  • Hardy and Littlewood, Some problems of Partitio Numerorum III (Acta Math. 44, 1923) — their Goldbach constant (singular series) is positive for every even number, the counting form of the fact that no finite set of wheels blocks a sum of two primes; the single-wheel and combined-cycle claims here state that fact without counting, in the stack picture
  • Goldbach's conjecture (Wikipedia) — states the conjecture whose equivalent forms this node proves; the stack and frontier forms are original

Related nodes

Connected in content but not by an arrow; each entry says how.

  • Schnirelmann proves every number is a sum of boundedly many primes; this node restates the two-prime case as stacks
  • SelbergTwinRails bounds the Goldbach pairs of one number from above; here they are the pairs of stacks building one target

Claims (9)

goldbach_iff_odd_goldbach
proved in Lean
Every even number above 2 is a sum of two primes exactly when every even number from 6 on is a sum of two odd primes.
/-- **Odd primes are enough.** The usual Goldbach conjecture holds exactly
when every even number from 6 on is a sum of two odd primes. -/
def goldbach_iff_odd_goldbach : Prop := goldbach ↔ odd_goldbach
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

stack_mod_three
proved in Lean
Every prime stack taller than 1 has a height leaving remainder 0 or 2 on division by 3, never 1.
/-- **The wheel of size 3.** Every stack taller than 1 has a height leaving
remainder 0 or 2 on division by 3, never 1 (remainder 1 would make its prime a
multiple of 3). -/
def stack_mod_three : Prop :=
  ∀ h : ℕ, is_stack h → 2 ≤ h → h % 3 ≠ 1
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.GoldbachStacks.stack_mod_three_holds ↗
wheel_no_gap
proved in Lean
At any single wheel, the heights whose stacks survive it, taken in pairs, reach every remainder, so no wheel on its own leaves a target unbuilt.
/-- **No single wheel forces a gap.** For every prime `q` and every remainder
`r` modulo `q`, there are two heights `a` and `b` modulo `q` whose stacks
survive the wheel of size `q` (twice the height plus 1 is not a multiple of
`q`) and whose sum leaves remainder `r`. -/
def wheel_no_gap : Prop :=
  ∀ q : ℕ, q.Prime → ∀ r : ZMod q,
    ∃ a b : ZMod q, 2 * a + 1 ≠ 0 ∧ 2 * b + 1 ≠ 0 ∧ a + b = r
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.GoldbachStacks.wheel_no_gap_holds ↗
wheels_no_gap
proved in Lean
For the combined cycle of all the wheels below any bound, every target position is the sum of two positions whose stacks survive every one of those wheels, so no finite set of wheels forces a gap.
/-- **No combined cycle forces a gap.** For every bound and every target
position `r` of the combined cycle of the wheels below that bound, there are
two positions `a` and `b` of the cycle whose stacks survive every one of those
wheels (on each wheel, twice the height plus 1 is not on the blocked
position) and whose sum is `r`. -/
def wheels_no_gap : Prop :=
  ∀ limit : ℕ, ∀ r : ZMod (primorial_modulus limit),
    ∃ a b : ZMod (primorial_modulus limit),
      (∀ q : active_primes limit,
        2 * crt_map limit a q + 1 ≠ 0 ∧ 2 * crt_map limit b q + 1 ≠ 0) ∧
      a + b = r
Rests on: CRT.crt_map_bijective
Statement in Conclusions.lean ↗
Proof: RNS.GoldbachStacks.wheels_no_gap_step ↗; joined to its inputs in Assemble.lean ↗
